answer: A stake-backed reputation bridge makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock real tokens before it can trade, like a willow bending but not breaking under weight — the stake bends with honest use and snaps back as slashing when fraud is proven. An attacker facing an ocean of honest staked agents must buy a matching stake for every fake identity, so creating thousands of Sybils costs thousands of stakes, while honest agents keep their locked funds and earn fees.
